os.description: The operating system its programs run on, spelled as Rust's `std::env::consts::OS` spells it (`windows`, `linux`, `macos`): which rules its paths follow.

arch.description: Its processor, spelled as `std::env::consts::ARCH` spells it.

local.description: Whether it shares the host's own files and paths, so that a folder the host names is the same folder there.

x-enum-labels.ready: It answers and takes what it is asked.
x-enum-labels.waiting: It answers, and waits for someone to approve this host there: [`EnvironmentInfo::detail`] says how.
x-enum-labels.down: It cannot be reached: [`EnvironmentInfo::detail`] says why.

state.description: Whether it can be used now.

detail.description: For [`State::Waiting`] and [`State::Down`]: what to do or what failed, in words for the person.

name.description: Its name: a word of lower-case letters, digits, `_` and `.`, 1 to 64. See [`capability`] for the ones the host maps.

facts.description: What the environment says of this capability (the shells it has, the folders its files are in, `read_only`), by name.

help.description: A line for people, and for the agent, on what the capability does here.

capabilities.description: What it offers now, each name once. A name missing here is not possible in this environment.

x-enum-labels.ready: It answers and takes what it is asked.
x-enum-labels.waiting: It answers, and waits for someone to approve this host there: [`EnvironmentInfo::detail`] says how.
x-enum-labels.down: It cannot be reached: [`EnvironmentInfo::detail`] says why.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes to answer. A longer file is refused `BAD_VALUE`, never cut.

path.description: The file's path. Folders on the way are made.

bytes.description: What it will hold: a file there is replaced.

len.description: Its length in bytes, for a file.

entries.description: Its entries, in the order the environment gives them.

len.description: Its length in bytes, for a file.

capability.description: The capability's name, one the environment declared.

arguments.description: The arguments, a JSON object as text; `{}` when the capability takes none.

text.description: The answer as text: what the agent reads, usually JSON.
